collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 16 major modern epidemics and pandemics from 1918 (Spanish flu) through 2025 — the union of (a) Wikipedia 'List of epidemics and pandemics' master-article 'Major epidemics and pandemics by death toll' top-19 list filtered to start-year ≥ 1918, (b) Wikipedia master-article 'Ongoing pandemics' list, and (c) the 8 WHO-declared Public Health Emergencies of International Concern (PHEIC) per the Wikipedia 'Public health emergency of international concern' article. For each event the staged row records the Start Year, Disease (pathogen or named disease), Affected Region (continent-or-global), Transmission Mode (from a closed 5-value taxonomy curator-derived from canonical WHO/CDC pathogen-transmission categories), and Specific Trigger (a brief curator-paraphrased phrase describing the documented spillover, contamination source, or causal narrative). The 16-row universe captures all modern events deemed 'major' by at least one of three authoritative master rules: the top-19 historical-death-toll list, the ongoing-pandemics list, or the formal WHO PHEIC declaration list. The schema is designed for benchmark evaluation: Epidemic is the PK lookup target; Start Year is exact-match numeric; Disease is exact-match from a finite (though somewhat open-ended) vocabulary; Affected Region is exact-match from a 6-value closed continent-or-global vocabulary; Transmission Mode is exact-match from a closed 5-value epidemiological taxonomy; Specific Trigger is semantic-match free-text.

Multi-source Tier B instance (source_count = 18 = 2 master + 16 per-event). The two master Wikipedia articles are the canonical compilations: source[0] for chronological enumeration and death-toll ranking, source[1] for WHO PHEIC declarations. The 16 per-event Wikipedia articles ground the answer-key Transmission Mode and Specific Trigger cells — each event's dedicated article supplies the transmission characteristic (from its Transmission / Epidemiology section) and the proximate causal narrative (from its Origin / Etiology / Lead section). Per-row cells: Epidemic name, Start Year, Disease, and Affected Region are verbatim/lightly-normalized from source[0]'s Event/Years/Disease/Location columns for 15 of 16 rows; for row 10 (2014 polio declaration) which has no source[0] chronological-table entry, the row is named per source[1]'s PHEIC declaration heading and Disease is set to 'Poliovirus' per source[1]'s pathogen identifier with per-pathogen support from source[11]. Transmission Mode is per-row grounded by the corresponding per-event source (source_urls[2-17]); the closed 5-value taxonomy maps each event to its dominant primary transmission characteristic. Specific Trigger is a 1-line (12-22 word) curator paraphrase of the corresponding per-event source's origin/etiology lead section. Cell-level audit can spot-check Epidemic/Year/Disease/Region cells against source[0] (master chronological tables); Transmission Mode and Specific Trigger cells can be spot-checked against the per-event source listed in this Roles block.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (16 major modern epidemics and pandemics 1918-2025 satisfying at least one of three authoritative-master rules: Wikipedia 'Major by death toll' top-19 filtered ≥1918 OR Wikipedia 'Ongoing pandemics' list OR WHO PHEIC declaration) is fully source-defined via the cited two master articles' lists; the triple-union filter rule is mechanical and source-grounded; per-row attribute cells are largely source-grounded via the master article's Event/Years/Disease/Location columns (15 of 16 rows; the 16th row '2014 polio declaration' is source-grounded via the PHEIC article's declaration list). Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical pandemics (1918 Spanish flu, HIV/AIDS, 2009 swine flu, COVID-19); mid-difficulty cells include major modern outbreaks (1957 Asian flu, 1968 Hong Kong flu, 2014 W. Africa Ebola, 2015 Zika); harder calibration cells include less-headline-grabbing events (Russia typhus 1918, Seventh cholera pandemic, 2014 polio PHEIC, Kivu Ebola, 2022 mpox Clade IIb vs 2023 Clade Ib distinction, 2024 Sudanese cholera). Row count (16) clears the 10-row gate comfortably.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected from a `causal` gap-1 saturation candidate slate (Health/Epidemiology, History/Military, Transportation/Aviation), choosing Health/Epidemiology with deep-dive on schema design (Schema A/B/C) and universe design (Option A/B/C); final choice Schema C (6 cols) + Option B universe (Master ∪ Ongoing ∪ PHEIC) + anchor year 1918.
- Category: causal (gap 1 before this staging — `causal` at 4 of 5 with crewed_spaceflight_fatal_incidents, modern_animal_extinctions_since_1900, politically_unstable_countries_per_continent_fsi_alert, modern_financial_crises_1929_2025; this instance brings causal to 5/5 SATURATING the category — FOURTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection, set_operation, set_filter) primary; temporal (gap 3) secondary because the Start Year column spans 1918-2024 providing a meaningful temporal axis. Per references/artifact-contract.md, causal pairs canonically with operation_type=projection (when the schema includes a Cause cell as one of the projected attributes); the db_analog 'SELECT ... FROM modern_epidemics_and_pandemics WHERE start_year >= 1918 AND ...' is the canonical causal-projection-over-triple-union-filtered-universe primitive.
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, multi-source; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 18 (2 master articles + 16 per-event articles after cycle-1 expansion to ground Transmission Mode and Specific Trigger answer-key cells).
- Expected shape: 16 rows × 6 columns; PK = Epidemic.
- Domain: Health/Epidemiology — first Health/Epidemiology subdomain (existing Health family is at 1 instance: `vitamins_top5_food_sources` Health/Nutrition; this instance extends Health from 1 to 2 instances with Epidemiology NEW subdomain).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) Transmission Mode is curator-derived from canonical WHO/CDC transmission categories. The 5-value taxonomy (Respiratory / Vector-borne / Direct contact / Water-or-Food-borne / Iatrogenic-or-Bioterrorism) is well-defined but some events have multiple transmission modes — e.g., HIV/AIDS is sexual + bloodborne + mother-to-child but is staged as 'Direct contact' per the dominant primary mode. (b) Affected Region distribution is heavily Worldwide (13 of 16) reflecting the modern-pandemic-scale nature of the universe; only 3 rows are sub-global (Russia typhus 1918 → Europe; Kivu Ebola → Africa; 2024 Sudanese cholera → Africa). (c) Specific Trigger cells are curator-paraphrased 1-line summaries of canonical epidemiological narratives; the master chronological tables do not have a Notes column, so trigger cells are semantic-match-evaluable rather than exact-match-from-source. (d) The 2014 polio declaration row lacks a dedicated chronological-table entry in source[0] and is source-grounded via source[1] (the PHEIC article) for name and PHEIC framing plus source[11] (Poliovirus per-pathogen article) for Transmission Mode and Disease grounding; this is the row with the most-distinct source path but is now fully source-grounded after cycle-1 source expansion. (e) The Iatrogenic-or-Bioterrorism Transmission Mode value is empty (zero events in the universe match this category); this is an empty closed-vocabulary slot that tests whether LLMs correctly avoid misclassification into the empty bucket. (f) Notable exclusions: SARS 2002-2004 is iconic and globally-impactful but excluded by strict Option B rule (not in Table[0] top-19, not in Table[8] ongoing, not formally PHEIC-declared since PHEIC declarations started 2009); same applies to 1976 first Ebola outbreak, 1979 Sverdlovsk anthrax leak, 1994 plague in India, and other notable but smaller-scale outbreaks.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets epidemics, pandemics, or health/disease events.

Why schema C (6 cols) rather than alternatives: deep-dive schema design considered 3 options. Schema A (4 cols, all exact-match-evaluable: Epidemic + Year + Pathogen Type + Transmission Mode) was the most automation-friendly but lost specificity (Pathogen Type would be heavily Virus-dominated with no Disease specificity). Schema B (5 cols: Epidemic + Year + Region + Cause Category + Specific Trigger, mirroring financial-crises pattern) balanced exact-match and semantic-match but did not include a Disease/Pathogen specificity column. Schema C (6 cols, adding Disease as a fully exact-match-evaluable column for biological specificity) was selected for benchmark richness. The Disease column tests pathogen-identification knowledge while the Transmission Mode column tests causal-mechanism classification; together they provide layered causal-attribution evaluation.

Why 'Modern era 1918-present' universe rather than alternatives: the user picked anchor year 1918 (Spanish flu) over alternatives 1900 (broader, includes pre-Spanish-flu plague waves) and 2009 (PHEIC-era only, smaller universe). The 1918 anchor matches the iconic 20th-century pandemic origin and excludes 19th-century cholera waves and earlier plague pandemics which cluster in pre-modern epidemiology. The triple-union rule (Master + Ongoing + PHEIC) was selected over Option A (Master + Ongoing only, ~10 rows tight at row-count floor) and Option C (chronological-table threshold ~25 rows with curator-defined death-toll threshold) for being authoritative-source-only (no curator-defined numeric thresholds) while comfortably clearing the row-count gate.

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: causal pairs reasonably with operation_type=projection per references/artifact-contract.md. The 5-attribute SELECT per row (Year, Disease, Region, Transmission Mode, Specific Trigger) over the triple-union-filtered universe is the canonical causal-projection-with-cause-attribution structure.

Domain selection: Health/Epidemiology — second Health instance after vitamins_top5_food_sources (Health/Nutrition); Epidemiology is a NEW subdomain within Health that complements the existing Nutrition angle. Per domain_taxonomy.md, the Health family expands from 1 to 2 instances with this staging.

Claim type: source_defined — the universe is fully defined by the union of three authoritative master lists (Wikipedia top-19 by death toll, Wikipedia ongoing pandemics, Wikipedia PHEIC declarations). The curator does NOT supplement the universe with non-master events. Specific Trigger cells are curator-paraphrased, but the universe rule itself is fully source-defined.

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 1): the cycle-1 audit returned 1 BLOCKING + 2 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE + 2 SUGGESTION findings. (a) BLOCKING — Transmission Mode and Specific Trigger answer-key cells were not source-grounded by the cycle-0 cited source set (only 2 master URLs). The audit found these were curator-derived from general WHO/CDC epidemiological categories and per-event narratives that were not in the cited URLs. The user picked Path A (expand sources to add per-event Wikipedia articles, preserving Schema C) over Path B (drop the two columns to a 4-col Schema-A-like result) and Path C (drop Specific Trigger only, keep Transmission Mode with per-pathogen sources). Resolved by adding 16 per-event Wikipedia article URLs to source_urls (1 per row; for the Russia typhus 1918 row which lacks a dedicated event article, the per-pathogen 'Epidemic typhus' article was used; for the 2014 polio row, the per-pathogen 'Poliovirus' article was used). source_count 2 → 18. Each Transmission Mode and Specific Trigger cell is now grounded by the corresponding per-event source's Transmission/Etiology/Origin/Lead sections. The per-event Roles block in source_coverage_notes lists which per-event URL grounds each row's answer-key cells. (b) HYGIENE #1 — Major-by-death-toll arithmetic understated: the cycle-0 prose said the top-19 component contributes 4 candidate memberships (Spanish flu, Russia typhus, Asian flu, Hong Kong flu), but the actual top-19 has 6 events with start-year ≥ 1918 (also HIV/AIDS at 1981-present and COVID-19 at 2019-present). Resolved by updating provenance arithmetic in temporal_note and _extraction_notes to '6 candidate memberships' and documenting the HIV/AIDS + COVID-19 dedup against the ongoing/PHEIC components. (c) HYGIENE #2 — Row 10 PK '2014 wild poliovirus international spread' was curator-constructed rather than source-verbatim. Resolved by renaming to '2014 polio declaration' which matches source[1]'s PHEIC article heading phrasing ('2014 polio declaration'). The CSV cell, draft.json's _extraction_notes and temporal_note, and curation.json's decision_log/normalization_decisions/open_questions were updated. (d) SUGGESTION #1 — empty Iatrogenic-or-Bioterrorism bucket: kept as a 5-value taxonomy with the empty slot retained per benchmark-design preference (closed-vocabulary integrity tests model-restraint against misclassification into the empty bucket). (e) SUGGESTION #2 — Disease column name imprecise for mixed disease/pathogen values: kept the name 'Disease' as source-shaped (the Wikipedia master article uses 'Disease' as the column header) rather than renaming to 'Disease or Pathogen' to maintain source-fidelity. Net cycle-1 changes: 16 per-event URLs added to source_urls; source_count 2 → 18; 1 PK rename (row 10: '2014 wild poliovirus international spread' → '2014 polio declaration'); 1 arithmetic fix (top-19 contribution 4 → 6); 1 source_coverage_notes Roles block rewrite to enumerate per-event Roles for all 18 sources; no CSV row count or distribution changes (still 16 rows, same Transmission Mode/Region distributions).

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 2): the cycle-2 audit returned 1 BLOCKING + 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE + 0 SUGGESTION findings. (a) BLOCKING — 3 Specific Trigger cells (rows 1, 5, 9) overstated or conflicted with their cycle-1-added per-event source articles. Specifically: (i) Row 1 Spanish flu trigger 'Avian-origin H1N1 influenza emerged during WWI troop movements' overstated origin certainty — the Spanish_flu article explicitly says geographic origin is indeterminate (supports Haskell County Kansas early cases + WWI troop movements but not a confident avian-origin causal statement). (ii) Row 5 Hong Kong flu trigger 'spread via international air travel' was unsupported — the Hong_Kong_flu article does not mention air travel as a spread mechanism but does support international spread including via U.S. troops returning from Vietnam War. (iii) Row 9 Western African Ebola trigger 'Fruit-bat-origin' directly contradicted the event article, which says fruit bats did not live near the initial transmission location in Meliandou Guinea and that the index case is suspected to have followed a child's contact with an insectivorous bat. Resolved by rewriting all 3 trigger cells to match the source-article wording: Row 1 → 'H1N1 pandemic spread from probable early U.S. cases through WWI-era troop movements; geographic origin remains uncertain'; Row 5 → 'H3N2 reassortant emerged in Hong Kong and spread internationally including via U.S. troops returning from the Vietnam War'; Row 9 → 'Index case in Meliandou Guinea suspected insectivorous-bat contact; spread via bodily fluid contact across Liberia and Sierra Leone'. (b) HYGIENE — 2 prose typo/staleness items: (i) draft.json::temporal_note contained a duplicate 'declaration declaration' typo in '2014 polio declaration declaration ongoing' introduced by the cycle-1 PK rename pass — fixed to '2014 polio declaration (ongoing)'. (ii) curation.json::normalization_decisions had a stale '2008 HIV/AIDS origin' year reference (HIV/AIDS pandemic is staged with Start Year 1981, not 2008) — fixed to 'HIV/AIDS origin'. Also updated the Specific Trigger example list in normalization_decisions to match the cycle-2 rewritten Trigger cells. Net cycle-2 changes: 3 Specific Trigger CSV cell rewrites (rows 1, 5, 9); 2 prose typo fixes (temporal_note + normalization_decisions); no source_urls / source_count / row count / schema / distribution changes (still 16 rows × 6 cols, source_count 18).

Post-audit (2026-05-14, cycle 3): cycle-3 audit verdict 'Ready' — 0 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. All cycle-2 trigger rewrites confirmed source-faithful (Spanish flu uncertain-origin + Kansas/WWI troop-spread framing; Hong Kong flu Vietnam-War-troops mechanism without air-travel claim; West African Ebola Meliandou + insectivorous-bat hypothesis); both prose typo fixes confirmed clean; opportunistic narrative scrubs confirmed consistent. Mechanical preflight passed: 16 rows × 6 cols, schema unchanged, PK unique, source_count = 18, chronological sort intact, closed Transmission Mode and Affected Region vocabularies intact. Instance marked accept-ready as of 2026-05-14. Total cycle count: 4 (cycle-0 staging + cycles 1-3 audit/repair). Universe stable at 16 events across all cycles; only repairs were source-set expansion (cycle-1: source_count 2 → 18) and per-cell source-grounding rigor on trigger wording (cycle-2: 3 rewrites). The instance SATURATES `causal` at 5/5 — FOURTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, and set_filter 5/5.
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is the 16 events satisfying at least one of three authoritative-master rules — (a) Wikipedia 'List of epidemics and pandemics' master article's 'Major epidemics and pandemics by death toll' top-19 list (Table[0] per pandas.read_html) filtered to start-year ≥ 1918, OR (b) the same master article's 'Ongoing pandemics' list (Table[8] per pandas.read_html), OR (c) the canonical 8 WHO Public Health Emergencies of International Concern (PHEIC) declarations enumerated in the Wikipedia 'Public health emergency of international concern' article. Dedup across the three sets yields 16 unique events: HIV/AIDS appears in (a)+(b) and counted once; COVID-19 appears in (a)+(b)+(c) and counted once; mpox PHEIC was declared twice (July 2022 Clade IIb and August 2024 Clade Ib) but these are captured as two distinct rows '2022-2023 mpox outbreak' (Table[7] chronological entry for Clade IIb) and '2023-2026 monkeypox epidemic' (Table[8] ongoing entry for Clade Ib). The 1918 anchor is the iconic Spanish flu pandemic that conventionally marks the start of modern epidemiology; pre-1918 events (1855-1960 Third plague pandemic, 1889-1890 Russian/Asiatic flu, 1846-1860 cholera pandemic, and earlier plague waves) are excluded by the temporal filter even if they extend into the 1918+ era. Epidemic name normalization: each event's Name is taken verbatim from the master chronological-tables' Event column where available (15 of 16 rows); for the 2014 polio declaration row which lacks a dedicated chronological-table entry, the canonical-form name '2014 polio declaration' is taken from the PHEIC article's heading phrasing for the May 2014 declaration. Start Year normalization: 4-digit integer of the first year in the master Years column (e.g., 'Hong Kong flu' Years='1968-1970' → Year 1968; 'HIV/AIDS pandemic' Years='1981-present' → Year 1981; 'COVID-19 pandemic' Years='2019[a]-present' → Year 2019; for the PHEIC-only polio row the year is 2014 per the May 2014 declaration date). Disease normalization: each event's Disease is taken verbatim from the master chronological-tables' Disease column where available (15 of 16 rows; values include 'Influenza A virus subtype H1N1', 'Typhus', 'HIV/AIDS', 'Cholera (El Tor strain)', 'Middle East respiratory syndrome / MERS-CoV', 'Ebola', 'Zika virus', 'COVID-19', 'Mpox', 'Monkeypox', 'Cholera'); for the 2014 polio row Disease = 'Poliovirus' per the PHEIC article's pathogen identifier. Affected Region normalization: each event's Region is normalized to a 6-value continent-or-global closed vocabulary (Worldwide / Africa / Americas / Asia / Europe / Oceania) curator-derived from the master Location column applying these rules: (i) source 'Worldwide' or 'Worldwide, primarily X' → 'Worldwide' (the source's primary framing); (ii) single-country source values within a single continent → that continent (Russia → Europe; DRC+Uganda → Africa; Sudan+SS+Chad → Africa); (iii) multi-continent source values → 'Worldwide'. Transmission Mode normalization: 5-value closed taxonomy with per-category definitions: (1) Respiratory — primary transmission via airborne droplets, aerosols, or respiratory secretions (6 events: 1918 Spanish flu H1N1, 1957 Asian flu H2N2, 1968 Hong Kong flu H3N2, 2009 swine flu H1N1pdm09, 2012+ MERS-CoV, 2019+ COVID-19 SARS-CoV-2); (2) Vector-borne — primary transmission via arthropod vectors (mosquitoes, lice, fleas, ticks) (2 events: 1918 Russia typhus body-louse-borne, 2015 Zika Aedes-mosquito-borne); (3) Direct contact — primary transmission via bodily fluid, sexual contact, or skin-lesion contact (5 events: HIV/AIDS sexual+bloodborne+vertical, West African Ebola bodily fluid, Kivu Ebola bodily fluid, 2022 mpox Clade IIb sexual networks, 2023+ mpox Clade Ib skin-lesion); (4) Water-or-Food-borne — primary transmission via contaminated water or food (3 events: Seventh cholera pandemic Vibrio cholerae waterborne, 2014 polio PHEIC poliovirus fecal-oral, 2024 Sudanese cholera Vibrio cholerae waterborne); (5) Iatrogenic-or-Bioterrorism — primary transmission via medical procedures, hospital settings, or deliberate release (0 events in the universe under this value; included in the closed vocabulary for completeness and to test whether LLMs avoid misclassification into the empty bucket). Assignment rules: where an event has multiple transmission modes, the dominant primary mode per canonical WHO/CDC classification is chosen (e.g., HIV/AIDS has sexual + bloodborne + mother-to-child but is staged as 'Direct contact' per its primary canonical mode); where the dominant mode differs from origin (Spanish flu has indeterminate geographic origin per its per-event source but human-to-human transmission via the Respiratory mode), Transmission Mode reflects the human-to-human transmission characteristic, not origin. Specific Trigger normalization: 1-line curator paraphrase (12-22 words) of canonical epidemiological documentation describing each event's spillover, contamination source, or proximate causal narrative. The paraphrase preserves substantive content while compressing per-event Wikipedia article narratives into a single-cell phrase. Examples (drawn verbatim from the staged CSV): 1918 Spanish flu → 'H1N1 pandemic spread from probable early U.S. cases through WWI-era troop movements; geographic origin remains uncertain'; HIV/AIDS origin in zoonotic SIV crossover → 'SIV from chimpanzees crossed to humans in Central Africa; first cases identified in 1981'; 2019 COVID-19 → 'SARS-CoV-2 emergence in Wuhan China in late 2019'. Sort order: the CSV is sorted **chronologically** by Start Year, matching the temporal-causal axis as the primary narrative dimension of this instance. Within the 1968 Hong Kong flu / 1961 Seventh cholera pandemic Year tie cluster (1961-1968 span), CSV ordering preserves source chronological-table order where applicable.
open_questions: 1. Whether SARS 2002-2004 should be included as a notable exclusion deserving explicit documentation in the open_questions section, or whether the strict Option B universe rule (no PHEIC pre-2009; not in top-19 by death toll due to only ~774 deaths) is sufficient justification for exclusion. Wikipedia's PHEIC article notes that SARS is 'automatically considered a PHEIC' under IHR (2005) without requiring an IHR decision; under that interpretation SARS could be included. Current staging excludes SARS under strict formal-declaration interpretation. 2. (Resolved in cycle-1) The 2014 polio declaration row was retained after cycle-1 source expansion strengthened its source-grounding via the per-pathogen 'Poliovirus' Wikipedia article (source_urls[11]) for Transmission Mode and Disease, plus the PHEIC article (source_urls[1]) for the declaration framing. 3. Whether the Transmission Mode column should be renamed to 'Cause Category' or 'Primary Causal Mechanism' to better align with the causal-category framing (currently 'Transmission Mode' which is mechanistic rather than causal). 4. Whether the Disease column should be split into Disease + Pathogen (current Disease values mix disease names like 'COVID-19' / 'HIV/AIDS' / 'Mpox' with pathogen names like 'Influenza A virus subtype H1N1' / 'Zika virus' — a mixed-content column). 5. Whether the heavily-Worldwide Affected Region distribution (13 of 16) is a feature or a bug — it reflects the modern-pandemic-scale universe but provides little Region-cell calibration signal. 6. Whether the empty Iatrogenic-or-Bioterrorism Transmission Mode value should be removed from the closed vocabulary (4-value taxonomy) or retained as an empty calibration slot (5-value taxonomy). Current staging retains it for completeness. 7. Whether Wikipedia's automatic-PHEIC rule (SARS, smallpox, wild-type polio, any new human influenza subtype) should be applied to broaden the universe; if so, the universe would expand to include SARS 2002-2004, smallpox post-1918 outbreaks, and various influenza-subtype-emergence events. 8. Whether the 2022-2023 mpox outbreak and 2023-2026 monkeypox epidemic should be merged into a single 'mpox global outbreaks 2022-present' row, or retained as two distinct rows per Wikipedia's chronological-table distinction (Clade IIb vs Clade Ib outbreaks). Current staging retains as two rows.
